record.paper_title: A collection of open problems in celebration of Imre Leader’s 60th birthday
record.context_brief: Monochromatic sums and products on infinite sets
record.original_question: Whenever the natural numbers are finitely colored, must there exist two infinite sets A and B of natural numbers such that the union {ab : a ∈ A, b ∈ B} ∪ {a + b : a ∈ A, b ∈ B} is monochromatic?

evidence.quote: Question 7.2 (F. Richter, Ultramath 2022, Pisa.). Suppose the natural numbers are coloured with finitely many colours. Must there exist two infinite sets of natural numbers, A and B, such that the set {ab : a ∈ A, b ∈ B} ∪ {a + b : a ∈ A, b ∈ B} is monochromatic?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{N}=\{1,2,3,\dots\}$ denote the set of positive integers. A finite coloring of $\mathbb{N}$ is a function $\chi:\mathbb{N}\to\{1,2,\dots,r\}$ for some positive integer $r$. A subset $S\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ is called monochromatic (with respect to $\chi$) if $\chi$ is constant on $S$.

Prove or disprove: for every finite coloring $\chi$ of $\mathbb{N}$, there exist two infinite subsets $A,B\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ such that the set
$$\{ab : a\in A,\ b\in B\}\ \cup\ \{a+b : a\in A,\ b\in B\}$$
is monochromatic.
artifact.category_tag: Ramsey theory: monochromatic sums and products
artifact.status_search_result: The question, posed by F. Richter at Ultramath 2022, appears to remain open. Recent surveys and papers on monochromatic sums and products (over $\mathbb{N}$ and $\mathbb{Q}$) discuss related results — e.g., it is known that one cannot in general find a single infinite sequence whose pairwise sums and products are all monochromatic, while the analogous infinite pattern over $\mathbb{Q}$ has been resolved — but the two-infinite-set formulation $\{ab\}\cup\{a+b\}$ over $\mathbb{N}$ does not appear to have been settled.

status_evidence.title: Monochromatic Sums and Products with Additive or Multiplicative Shifts in Natural Numbers
status_evidence.snippet: Studies recent progress on monochromatic sum-product patterns; cites Richter's question as motivation among open problems.
status_evidence.claim: The two-infinite-set sum-product question is treated as an open problem in current literature.

status_evidence.title: Monochromatic sums and products in N (Annals of Mathematics)
status_evidence.snippet: Resolves the {x+y, xy} pair question but leaves stronger infinite versions open.
status_evidence.claim: Known results address weaker/finite patterns; the infinite two-set version remains open.

status_evidence.title: Monochromatic Sums and Products over Q
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes partition regularity of sum-product configurations over the rationals.
status_evidence.claim: Analogous infinite-pattern result is known over Q but not over N.
